column3: Conjecture 1.2 and following paragraph explicitly cite Pokrovskiy's counterexample for every t>=3. Replaying or shrinking that public construction cannot earn credit; equality wording is also only an extremal bound convention.

The r=2 matching reduction does not extend to r-partite hypergraph transversals. A full proof must control all independence numbers and all r, not just complete graphs; source Conjecture 1.1 gives exactly this obstruction.

Need uniform adversarial coloring control at the sharp random-graph common-neighborhood threshold. The source's r=2 update cannot supply arbitrary r; fixed graph enumeration cannot certify an a.a.s. assertion.

An orbifold-action classification must exclude larger actions for every admissible genus, not only construct the displayed complete bipartite examples. Conjectures 1.3/5.5 depend on the exceptional-genus table and minimal/extendable action definitions; not fully audited.

Deleting k-1 colors reduces to the single-color tree-cover conjecture and saves no extra tree unconditionally. Source Conjecture 1.2 includes k=1; proving the k>r/4 regime again would only repeat a cited result.
Source Conjecture 1.4 needs the final improvement from 2r-1 to 2r-2 for arbitrary colors. Star covers and duplicating the smaller side do not give that saving; r<=5 is already cited as known.

Source Proposition 4.11 supplies a degree-bounded factor, but not its k-edge-colorability. The obstruction is class-II factors; a switching argument must preserve saturation off every k-optimal D. Definition and factor dependencies incompletely audited.

Each new edge gives only an O(n^2) potential bound. Source Conjecture 1 requires little-o for each fixed r>=5; the near-quadratic constructions show why finite stabilization runs cannot settle the asymptotic gap.

The universal eventual quantifier requires a uniform upper bound matching the recursively constructed q(n). Checking finitely many n cannot disprove or prove eventual equality; definition of union-free allows unions of arbitrary subfamilies, not just pairs.

Transfer matrices indexed by exposed matching/dominating states could compare helicene with every legal turn word. One must prove a common invariant cone or local replacement inequality including both turn directions; recurrences for individual chain types alone do not prove Conjecture 5.1.

Rational density alone is insufficient: the locus of tuples lying on some effective equivalent divisor need not be a finite closed polyhedral union. Source Proposition 3.3 handles dimension one; higher-dimensional uniform finiteness is the missing compactness step.

Counting tangent intersections must also certify absence of all secant intersections away from the tangent developable. Arbitrary linear-space examples miss the cuspidal-projection hypothesis; source Conjecture 8.4.1 is tied to the cusp-bound program.

Both irreducible equality and multiplicativity through nonsplit t-module extensions are required. Leading-coefficient invertibility gives only the source example; the saturation-growth definition and extension control remain unaudited.

Total-clique bounds give the claimed estimate only for much larger k than c log t. Full scope needs a uniform transition bound over all minor-free graphs and t; a fixed t certificate cannot provide universal constants.

Source Proposition 21 proves only k=t-1. For general k>=lambda t, clique-sum constructions explain the lower bound but do not classify extremizers; exhibiting failures for small lambda cannot negate the existential lambda.

This is the minimization version of Frankl's conjecture, explicitly equivalent in the source. Integer-program instances would only recheck finite cases; the {empty set} convention also requires care and cannot generate credit as a wording repair.

Cloning elements proves one inequality; deleting a coordinate can merge distinct sets and destroy the extremal value. Source Theorem 2.4 equates the f and g stabilization assertions, but does not supply the missing dimension-free compression.

Finite-order entropy optimization cannot show the global maximizing measure is non-Markov of every order or unique. Need strict improvements at all orders plus control of weak limits and ascendancy continuity; source Conjecture 6.5 remains only a located statement here.

The source quantity minimizes equal counts on each retained level, not unrestricted cutset cardinality as the record suggests. Kruskal-Katona shadow constraints may permit a recursion; exact quantification of n>>m and endpoint conventions must be reconciled first.

Source Conjecture 5 uses restricted u-hat rather than the record's unadorned u. Exact coset formulas and admissible m,h must be fixed before a subset enumeration; correcting that notation would earn no discovery credit.

Prime-order polynomial-method bounds and the source's cited h=2 result do not handle every h in arbitrary finite abelian groups. Need a torsion-sensitive restricted-sumset compression; checking cyclic groups alone misses full scope.

The rank-two elementary-abelian count is source-internal evidence only. The desired bound must control every abelian invariant-factor type and all m together; no additive count formula for mixed prime-power factors is established here.

Subset-sum dynamic programming could find a finite cyclic witness below the divisor construction. Proving equality for all n needs a structural lower bound for composite groups; source Theorem 16 covers prime order already, so that case is not creditable.

Source Theorem 4 explicitly refutes Jang-Kim with a quadratic-order indecomposable. Exact displayed bound comparison gives positive gap 215302457; indecomposability and negative-norm minimization were not replayed. A smaller example would remain an instance of a public refutation.

An induction must balance maximum triangle-independent sets with maximum cuts simultaneously; separate sharp bounds do not add to n^2/4. Source improves only to 4403n^2/15000; current resolution and dependency audits are missing.

Bezout bounds alone control total degree but not how many complete-intersection points lie on each hyperplane. Need a residual-ideal separator lower bound uniform in all fields and degrees; source Proposition 6.8 covers nested Cartesian sets only.

Source identifies this as the TFNP conjecture in Herbrand-search form. Diagonalizing over proofs does not yield the required polynomial nonreducibility against every problem provably total in T; no small certificate program survives.

Product extensions prove subadditivity; the missing direction requires separating nonnegative factor resources across both slack-matrix blocks. Source Corollary 2.4 treats a simplex factor only. Degenerate factors or slack conventions are not substantive discoveries.

Source pi is a nonrepetitive vertex chromatic number, while the record calls it an index. Need the directed Jaco adjacency definition and a coloring avoiding repetitions on every simple path for all m,c,n; a repaired parameter name is no credit.

Primary Conjecture 1.1 includes the omitted delta>=n/4 condition. The following paragraph and Figure 1 already supply two counterexamples; Theorem 1.2 proves a modified version. Refuting the record by an arbitrary star would merely exploit its missing hypothesis.

Incidence reductions give expansion exponents far below 2-epsilon; full scope requires arbitrary finite complex sets for every non-additive non-multiplicative rational map. Pole-domain repairs or a single special map would not resolve the source conjecture.

A small cubic graph plus a proper vertex coloring without rainbow P4 could refute either the bound or equality characterization. Full verification needs all P4s and an exact optimum, not just one coloring below the upper bound; bipartite equality is already source-internal.

For each polygon size the assertion existentially selects a puncture location. A large flip distance for one pair is only a lower bound; full diameter equality needs a uniform upper bound and all placement constraints. Enumerating one polygon does not settle every n>=13.

Logarithmic differentiation reduces critical points to F(alpha)=(-A ln(10)/10)b_eff P(1-P)-2alpha. Four binary64 signs for high-rise parameters alternate +,-,+,-, suggesting two local maxima under Eq.15 degree convention. Eq.12 omits that conversion; interval certification, source convention reconciliation and closest successor/prior checks are still missing.

Iterated balanced cycle blow-ups give the proposed lower density, not the matching universal upper bound. Source fixed-k=5 flag-algebra result and its total-induced-cycle theorem do not settle every k>=5.

Euler sparsity combined with source Theorem 1.3 leaves a coefficient above 3/10. A full result needs stronger reducible configurations or a genuinely sharper induced-forest theorem; checking the dodecahedron just repeats the tight example.

Divisibility is necessary but a fractional clique decomposition does not itself give an exact edge partition at the sharp threshold. Absorption plus a sharp fractional threshold for every r is required; bounded clique packing cannot prove eventual n0(r).

Only finitely many face sizes remain after the cited >=18 theorem, but each size includes infinitely many plane graphs. Need complete reducibility/discharging for the remaining sizes; verifying 16,17 again repeats this source's theorem.

Three points determine a circle, giving only an O(n^3/k^3) count. The extra factor n saving requires a strong incidence bound uniform for polynomially rich circles; finite configurations cannot establish the epsilon-dependent asymptotic constants.

Source Theorem 3.10 gives k(k+1)(k+2)(5k+11)/24 for s=2k+1, algebraically the exact displayed formula. k=0..100 cross-multiplication checked; theorem's combinatorial proof and dependencies not independently audited. This is a public source theorem, not a new candidate.

Known estimates for individual covering minima lose dimension factors when multiplied. Source Conjecture 4.7 is genuinely simultaneous over all convex bodies and all dimensions; simplex or symmetric-body instances cannot settle it.

Normality and amenability identify the intersection over measures only conditionally in Corollary 7.3. Need each measure's convolution-return ratio subgroup to contain every amenable normal subgroup; a favorable generating measure is not enough.

An exact resonant integer quadruple above the proposed horizontal bound could be a short counterexample, but membership in Lambda and primitive versus nonprimitive conventions must be checked from the source equation. Finite search below a height cannot prove the uniform b^4 bound.

The easy inequality porous<=ordinary exponential<=domination gives only one implication. A witness needs ordinary/exponential equality for every induced subgraph but a porous gap somewhere; testing only G loses the hereditary quantifier.

Encoding A as colors gives bipartite color classes with at least n edges and bounded aggregate degrees, not necessarily matchings. Drisko's theorem on matching color classes cannot be applied directly; need a new augmenting argument handling adjacent edges of a color.

A maximal rainbow matching's vertices can hit roughly 2(k-1)d edges per color, losing a factor two. Common bipartitions and integrality of d need source conventions checked; the d=1 obstruction alone does not negate the intended integer d>1 claim.

Theorem 4.4 gives a bound depending on maximum family rank r; Conjecture 4.5 needs m0(t) independent of r and arbitrary family. Exact strong/extrastrong property definitions and an r-free compression are missing; selecting bounded rank only repeats a known theorem.

Need the branching-random-walk hypotheses and topology/mode of convergence before proving the fixed-k cluster law. Tightness estimates and Brownian analogues alone do not identify the unique limiting law; source Conjecture 5.5 is not an almost-sure convergence theorem.

The source states it proves the pineapple extremizer only for sufficiently large n. That does not clear the unrestricted all-order record; finite residual classification and precise pineapple definition remain. The public asymptotic theorem cannot be counted again.

For each order-six Latin square, failure is feasibility of a rational linear system forcing at most five nonnegative lines under zero-sum weights. A complete witness would list the square and rational weights; a positive proof would require all isomorphism classes with exact infeasibility certificates. Source Proposition 6.1 addresses strictness only, not the target property.
